jade-cta.$description: Jade CTA — Primary CTA buttons, active links, key interactive highlights — jade against black in the hero and against white in body sections maintains equal visual force without changing hue

mint-surface.$description: Mint Surface — Card backgrounds, feature highlight areas — pastel counterpoint to jade that reads as 'selected' or 'active' without the full saturation of CTA jade

forest.$description: Forest — Card accent backgrounds, deep green surface variant

badge-leaf.$description: Badge Leaf — Blog/category badge backgrounds — near-white green tint that signals categorization without demanding attention

badge-text.$description: Badge Text — Badge text and border on leaf background — dark enough on #d5f8e0 to pass contrast without going full black

void.$description: Void — Hero background, primary text, button borders, icon fills — the dominant surface and text color simultaneously; this dual role is the system's core tension

paper.$description: Paper — Section backgrounds, card surfaces, nav background

fog.$description: Fog — Secondary button fill, subtle input backgrounds

ash.$description: Ash — Card background variant, divider surfaces

cool-grey.$description: Cool Grey — Borders, nav dividers, separator lines

slate.$description: Slate — Subheadings, secondary headings, muted heading text

stone.$description: Stone — Body secondary text, muted links

ink.$description: Ink — Link text, image overlay text

charcoal.$description: Charcoal — Nav secondary elements, supplementary UI chrome

stk-bureau.$description: All display and hero headlines exclusively. Weight 300 at 70-100px with -0.04 to -0.05em tracking is the signature voice — letters crowd each other at scale, creating mass through density rather than weight. Nothing else in the system uses this font.

abc-social.$description: Everything else: nav (14px/500), body copy (16-18px/400), buttons (14-16px/500-600), badges (12px/500), eyebrow labels (11px/500 at +0.175em tracking). The +0.175-0.25em tracking on small caps/eyebrows is the only place the system opens up letter-spacing — everywhere else it's tight or default.
